title: Sections and stalks of the sharpened affine monoid structure sheaf
statement:
Let $P$ be a fine commutative monoid, written additively, let $X=\operatorname{Spec}_{\mathrm{mon}}P$, and let $\overline{\mathcal M}_P$ be the sheafification of the quotient of its monoid structure sheaf by units [def-trf-fine-fan-blowup]. For $a\in P$, write $P_a=P-\mathbf N a\subset P^{\mathrm{gp}}$. For a prime ideal $\mathfrak p\subset P$, put $F=P\setminus\mathfrak p$ and $P_{\mathfrak p}=P-F\subset P^{\mathrm{gp}}$. There are canonical identifications
$$\Gamma(D(a),\overline{\mathcal M}_P)=P_a/P_a^\times,\qquad (\overline{\mathcal M}_P)_{\mathfrak p}=P_{\mathfrak p}/P_{\mathfrak p}^\times.$$
The restriction and germ homomorphisms in these identifications are induced by localization, and the canonical section of $p\in P$ has zero germ at $\mathfrak p$ if and only if $p\notin\mathfrak p$.

source.place: Expose VIII, 3.1.3 and Remark 3.1.4(i),(iii), printed pp.98--99; localization and sharpening in 3.1.1--3.1.2.

proof.text: Use the monoid, prime-ideal, localization and topology definitions in [def-trf-fine-fan-blowup]. For $a\in P$, put $F_a=\{c\in P:\exists d\in P,\ n\in\mathbf N,\ c+d=na\}$. This contains $0,a$, is closed under addition, and has the face property: if $c+e\in F_a$, an equation $c+e+d=na$ puts both $c$ and $e$ in $F_a$. Hence $\mathfrak m_a=P\setminus F_a$ is a proper prime ideal: adding an arbitrary element to a nonmember of $F_a$ cannot enter $F_a$, and its complement is closed under addition. In particular $\mathfrak m_a\in D(a)$. If $\mathfrak q\in D(a)$, then every $c\in F_a$ avoids $\mathfrak q$: otherwise $c+d=na$ belongs to $\mathfrak q$, whereas all multiples of $a$ avoid it. Thus $\mathfrak q\subseteq\mathfrak m_a$.

source.place: VIII 3.1.2--3.1.4(i),(iii), printed p.98; explicit face calculation

proof.text: Every basic neighborhood $D(c)$ of $\mathfrak m_a$ has $c\in F_a$, so the previous calculation gives $D(a)\subseteq D(c)$. Since the $D(c)$ form a basis, every open neighborhood of $\mathfrak m_a$ contains $D(a)$. Consequently every open cover $D(a)=\bigcup_i U_i$ has a member equal to $D(a)$: choose a member containing $\mathfrak m_a$. This also treats $a=0$, for which $F_0=P^\times$ and $D(0)=X$.

source.place: VIII Remark 3.1.4(iii), printed p.98; triviality of covers of basic opens

proof.text: Let $Q$ be the presheaf of commutative monoids $Q(U)=\mathcal M_P(U)/\mathcal M_P(U)^\times$. Restriction sends units to units because it sends an equation $u+v=0$ to the same equation, so these quotient restrictions are well defined. By [def-trf-fine-fan-blowup], its monoid sheafification is $\overline{\mathcal M}_P$. Apply [lem-trf-commutative-monoid-sheafification]: the underlying set presheaf $A=|Q|$ has set sheafification $B=|\overline{\mathcal M}_P|$, with the same unit $\eta:A\to B$. Work in one universe large enough for the opens of $X$ and these coefficient sets; its open site is small there.

The unit $\eta:A\to B=A^\#$ is locally bijective by [lem-weil-pbc-large-set-sheafification], as follows directly from its stated criterion. First, for any sheaf $H$, its sheafification unit $\eta_H:H\to H^\#$ is invertible: the universal property [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] gives $r:H^\#\to H$ with $r\eta_H=1_H$, and uniqueness after precomposition with $\eta_H$ gives $\eta_Hr=1_{H^\#}$. Naturality gives $\eta^\#\eta=\eta_B\eta$; uniqueness after precomposition with $\eta$ then gives $\eta^\#=\eta_B$, which is invertible by the preceding argument. The cited criterion therefore applies to $\eta$. In explicit terms, each section of $B(U)$ lifts to $A$ on an open cover of $U$, and any two sections of $A(U)$ with the same image agree on an open cover of $U$.

source.place: Tags 00WH (proposition-sheafification-adjoint) and 00WK (lemma-sections-sheafification); local-bijection criterion supplied by the cited existing large-set node.

proof.text: Apply these two local conditions on $U=D(a)$. Every covering family has a member $D(a)$ itself by Step 2. A local lift over that member is a lift over $D(a)$, proving surjectivity of $\eta_{D(a)}$; local equality on that member is equality on $D(a)$, proving injectivity. The monoid unit thus identifies $\overline{\mathcal M}_P(D(a))$ with $Q(D(a))=P_a/P_a^\times$, since $\mathcal M_P(D(a))=P_a$ by [def-trf-fine-fan-blowup]. The bijective monoid homomorphism is a monoid isomorphism: its inverse preserves sums and zero by injectivity.

For a prime $\mathfrak p$, its complement $F$ is a face: if $c+d\in F$ then neither $c$ nor $d$ can belong to the ideal $\mathfrak p$. Choose finite monoid generators $e_1,\ldots,e_r$ of $P$, and let $b$ be the sum of those generators lying in $F$, with empty sum $0$. Every expression for $f\in F$ uses only such generators, by the face property. Thus $F$ is generated by them. Primality gives $D(b)=\bigcap_{e_i\in F}D(e_i)=\bigcap_{f\in F}D(f)$, so $D(b)$ is the smallest open neighborhood of $\mathfrak p$. Furthermore $P_b=P-F$: since $b\in F$ the first monoid is contained in the second, while $-e_i=(b-e_i)-b\in P_b$ for each selected generator, so all of $F$ is invertible in $P_b$. Every germ at $\mathfrak p$ therefore has a representative on $D(b)$, and two representatives there have equal germs only if they agree on $D(b)$, since no smaller neighborhood exists. Step 5 now identifies the stalk with $P_b/P_b^\times=(P-F)/(P-F)^\times$.

source.place: VIII 3.1.2 and Remark 3.1.4(ii),(iii), printed p.98; smallest-neighborhood stalk computation

proof.text: The identifications in Step 5 are made by the quotient-presheaf unit, which commutes with every restriction. If $D(c)\subseteq D(a)$, then $\mathfrak m_c\in D(a)$, so $a\in F_c$ by Step 1. An equation $a+d=nc$ shows $-a=d-nc\in P_c$. Hence the restriction $P_a\to P_c$ exists and sends $p-ma$ to the same group-completion element $p-ma$; by [def-trf-fine-fan-blowup] it is precisely the unsharpened restriction. Passing to quotients sends $\operatorname{cl}(p-ma)$ to $\operatorname{cl}(p-ma)$, because units map to units. For $\mathfrak p\in D(a)$, the smallest neighborhood $D(b)$ of Step 6 is contained in $D(a)$; applying this formula to that restriction gives exactly the germ map induced by $P_a\to P-F$. Thus both the restriction and germ identifications are canonical and induced by localization.

source.place: VIII 3.1.2--3.1.4, printed p.98; compatibility of localization restrictions and germs

proof.text: The germ of the canonical section $p\in P$ is consequently $\operatorname{cl}(p)\in(P-F)/(P-F)^\times$. By the sharpening definition [def-trf-fine-fan-blowup], this class is zero exactly when $p$ is a unit in $P-F$. If $p\in F$, its inverse $-p$ lies in $P-F$. Conversely, if $p+(q-f)=0$ with $q\in P$ and $f\in F$, equality inside $P^{\mathrm{gp}}$ gives $p+q=f$ in $P$, using integrality. The face property of $F$ gives $p\in F$. Thus the zero-germ condition is equivalent to $p\in F$, or $p\notin\mathfrak p$, as required.

source.place: VIII 3.1.1--3.1.4(i), printed p.98; units in localization and sharpening

proof_origin.place: Expose VIII, 3.1.1--3.1.4, printed p.98; trivial-cover argument expanded using Stacks 00WH, 00WK and 00YR and the cited general set-sheafification criterion.

lean.statement: theorem affineFan_localization_sections (P : Type u) [CommMonoid P] (hP : IsFine P) : ∃ (sections : ∀ a : P, (affine P).presheaf.obj (op (basicOpen a)) ≃* Associates (Algebra.faceLocalization P (Submonoid.powers a))) (stalks : ∀ x : MonoidPrime P, stalk (affine P).presheaf x ≃* Associates (Algebra.faceLocalization P (Submonoid.closure {a : P | a ∉ x.carrier}))), (∀ a p : P, ∃ q : Algebra.faceLocalization P (Submonoid.powers a), q.val = Algebra.GrothendieckGroup.of p ∧ sections a ((affine P).presheaf.map (homOfLE le_top).op (affineSection P p)) = Associates.mk q) ∧ (∀ (a b : P) (h : basicOpen b ≤ basicOpen a) (q : Algebra.faceLocalization P (Submonoid.powers a)), ∃ r : Algebra.faceLocalization P (Submonoid.powers b), r.val = q.val ∧ sections b ((affine P).presheaf.map (homOfLE h).op ((sections a).symm (Associates.mk q))) = Associates.mk r) ∧ (∀ (a : P) (x : MonoidPrime P) (hx : x ∈ basicOpen a) (q : Algebra.faceLocalization P (Submonoid.powers a)), ∃ r : Algebra.faceLocalization P (Submonoid.closure {p : P | p ∉ x.carrier}), r.val = q.val ∧ stalks x (germ (affine P).presheaf (basicOpen a) x hx ((sections a).symm (Associates.mk q))) = Associates.mk r) ∧ (∀ (x : MonoidPrime P) (p : P), affineGerm x p = 1 ↔ p ∉ x.carrier)
